best_for: Photographers and designers on Windows or Linux who want a fast free viewer that opens RAW and PSD files and compares shots side by side.
description:
nomacs, also called Image Lounge, is a free image viewer released as open source under the GPL-3.0. The project keeps its code on GitHub and has a chat room on Matrix.

A file panel lets you jump between folders without leaving the viewer. Inside a folder you can filter which images show by a word in the file name or by a regular expression. Turn on the cache and you can flip from one picture to the next with no wait. Beyond the basics, you can tune gamma and exposure, and the pseudo color tool turns a photo into a false color image. If you spot a bug or want a feature, you can report it on the project's tracker.

points.title: Opens RAW and PSD
points.text: Besides common formats, nomacs views camera RAW and Photoshop files, and can browse images inside zip and Office files.

points.title: Compare two shots in sync
points.text: You can link several nomacs windows so zoom and pan move together, or overlay one image on another at a chosen opacity. Handy for picking the sharper of two frames.

points.title: Light edits only
points.text: It crops, resizes, rotates and adjusts colors. Panels show thumbnails, metadata and a histogram, and you can add notes to images. It is a viewer first, not a photo editor.

points.title: Free for any use
points.text: nomacs is GPL-3.0 and free for private and commercial use.

points.title: Windows and Linux here
points.text: The Windows MSI installs machine-wide, x64 only, at 3.22.5, and the Windows listing keeps 7 versions. The Flathub build is verified and already at 3.23, with only the current release listed. No Mac build is listed here.
